demographic_risk_rules.reason: Reproductive-age female with abdominal pain -- pregnancy/ectopic pregnancy must be considered regardless of whether it has been explicitly mentioned yet.

medication_risk_rules.reason: Anticoagulant use substantially raises the risk and severity of intracranial hemorrhage presenting as headache.
Antiplatelet/anticoagulant/NSAID use raises the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
Known diabetes on glucose-lowering medication raises the prior for a glucose-related emergency (DKA or hypoglycemia) in this presentation.
Glucose-lowering medication (insulin or a sulfonylurea) known to cause hypoglycemia raises the prior for a hypoglycemic episode in this presentation, especially with reduced oral intake.

note: These rules only ever ADD a safety finding when the case is already plausible for that diagnosis (chief-complaint-tag-gated, same as the symptom/vital-sign red flags in critical_conditions.json) -- never a blanket check across unrelated presentations (spec section 5's 'never blanket-test' requirement applies here too).
